# 12 Days to Deming

> The complete text of Dr Henry R. Neave's 12 Days to Deming — a free, interactive active-learning course on W. Edwards Deming's management philosophy, published online with the author's permission.

## Pages

- [About this edition: why and how this web adaptation was built](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/about-this-edition.html): Why Lee Durbin adapted 12 Days to Deming for the web, what changed from Neave's original PDFs, and the author's personal blessing for this edition.
- [What this course covers: who it's for and how the 12 days break down](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/what-this-course-covers.html): A day-by-day breakdown of what 12 Days to Deming covers, who each part suits, and the two hands-on projects at its core.
- [Welcome: the story of W. Edwards Deming and what this course covers](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/welcome.html): How Deming transformed Japanese industry from 1950, what this course covers, and why practitioners recommend it — introduced by Dr Henry Neave.
- [12 Days to Deming: Dr Henry Neave's free interactive Deming course](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/index.html): Henry Neave's 12 Days to Deming, adapted for the web: a free, interactive course on W. Edwards Deming's management philosophy, published with his blessing.
- [Accessibility features of the 12 Days to Deming web edition](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/accessibility.html): The accessibility features built into this course — skip links, a dyslexia font, keyboard navigation, ARIA labelling — and what's still on the roadmap.
- [Share your experience of 12 Days to Deming](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/share-your-experience.html): Tell us how 12 Days to Deming has helped you — a short, optional form, with the choice to be quoted publicly or to stay anonymous.
- [Privacy: what this site collects, and what it deliberately doesn't](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/privacy.html): What 12 Days to Deming collects about your visit — cookie-free analytics, optional feedback forms — and exactly what it doesn't, explained in plain terms.
- [Changes from the source: how this edition differs from Neave's PDFs](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/changes-from-source.html): The two material differences between this web edition and Neave's original PDF course, plus a full, dated changelog of every departure from the source.
- [FAQ: cost, length, prerequisites, and key concepts in 12 Days to Deming](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/faq.html): Answers to common questions about 12 Days to Deming: cost, time commitment, prerequisites, and core concepts like the Red Bead Experiment.

## Day 1: The Overture

- [Day 1: The Overture — a first taste of Deming's approach to management](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/01-overture.html): Neave's Overture previews the whole course's themes, explaining why active learning — not just reading — is how you'll learn Deming's management theory.
- [Day 1: How Deming was rediscovered, from Nashua to the four-day seminars](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/02-rediscovered.html): How Nashua's Bill Conway discovered W Edwards Deming via Japan's Deming Prize, sparking the four-day seminars and the British Deming Association.
- [Day 1: Why 'understanding variation' isn't traditional statistics](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/03-statistics.html): Neave reassures statistics-averse readers: this course needs no probability or hypothesis tests — just Shewhart's idea of understanding variation.
- [Day 1: Recommended Deming books and videos beyond the course text](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/04-resources.html): Neave's reading list beyond the course text: Out of the Crisis, The New Economics, and video recommendations including The Deming of America.
- [Day 1: How this course's Activities and Pauses for Thought work](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/05-activities.html): Explains the course's four levels of interactive exercise — Pauses for Thought, Activities, Major Activities and Projects — and their colour conventions.
- [Day 1: A day-by-day outline of all 12 days of this course](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/06-outline.html): A preview of what's ahead: the Red Beads and Funnel Experiments, the 14 Points, Gallery Furniture, and the System of Profound Knowledge across 12 days.
- [Day 1: Why Deming's work is a theory of management, not 'quality'](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/07-quality-theory.html): A word-count from The Deming of America shows Deming said 'management' and 'theory' far more than 'quality' — his real subject was a theory of management.
- [Day 1: What first attracted Henry Neave to Deming's work](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/08-attraction.html): Henry Neave explains what drew him to Deming: not the statistics, but the humanity, logic, and systems-thinking behind his approach to management.
- [Day 1: How Deming's philosophy differs from conventional management](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/09-different.html): A rapid-fire list of what makes Deming's philosophy different: intrinsic motivation, driving out fear, cooperation over competition, and no targets.
- [Day 1: Famous wrong predictions, and why new ideas get rejected](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/10-relief.html): Classic wrong predictions, from the telephone to the Beatles, illustrate why radically different ideas like Deming's are so often dismissed at first.
- [Day 1: The Deming story, from Shewhart's mentee to Japan and beyond](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/11-deming-story.html): Deming's life story: mentored by Walter Shewhart in the 1920s, teaching Japan's industrialists in 1950, the 'wasted years', and his Profound Knowledge.
- [Day 1: Why most problems come from the system, not the individual](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/12-intro-activity.html): Neave introduces Deming's provocative claim that the system, not the individual, causes the vast majority of problems, ahead of Major Activity 1-f.
- [Day 1: Major Activity 1-f — contrasting environments and behaviour](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-01/13-major-activity.html): Major Activity 1-f: compare how you'd behave across ten pairs of opposite environments, from trust vs distrust to war vs peace, to explore system effects.

## Day 2: The Experiment on Red Beads

- [Day 2: Run charts, and why every sales wiggle looks meaningful](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/01-run-charts.html): A monthly sales example shows how a run chart makes trends visible, and how management reacts to random monthly ups and downs as if each were meaningful.
- [Day 2: Introducing Deming's Red Beads Experiment](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/02-intro-to-the-red-beads-experiment.html): Neave introduces Deming's famous Red Beads Experiment, confessing that he too was sceptical of this 'stupidly simple' exercise before he saw it work.
- [Day 2: How the Red Beads Experiment is run, step by step](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/03-a-brief-overview.html): A full walkthrough of the Red Beads Experiment: Foreman, Willing Workers and Inspectors, training, quotas, and firing the 'worst' performers by name.
- [Day 2: The Red Beads control chart — all just common-cause variation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/04-our-first-control-chart.html): Plotting the Red Beads data on a control chart shows every result within the limits, proving the workers' scores were common-cause variation, not skill.
- [Day 2: Inside the Red Beads apparatus and its control limits](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/05-the-truth-the-whole-truth-and-nothing-but.html): The mechanics of the Red Beads apparatus and training procedure, framed through the 'All-Knowing' vs 'Un-Knowing' lens, plus how to compute control limits.
- [Day 2: Play the Foreman, reacting to the Red Beads results](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/06-your-turn.html): Now you play the Foreman: react to each Red Beads result as it comes in, then see how easily you invented explanations for pure random variation.
- [Day 2: Best and worst-ever Red Beads results, and what they don't prove](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/07-some-recollections.html): Neave's Red Beads recollections: the best-ever result (professional statisticians) and worst-ever (a Madrid seminar) — and why neither proves anything.
- [Day 2: Major Activity — writing up the Red Beads Experiment's lessons](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/08-major-activity.html): Day 2's Major Activity: summarise the lessons from the Red Beads Experiment, then reflect on times you've been the Willing Worker or the Foreman.
- [Day 2: Postscript — a second Madrid result, and prepping for Day 3](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-02/09-postscript.html): The rest of the Spaniards' story from a second Madrid seminar, a colleague's Red Beads wrap-up brief, and how to prepare for Day 3's Funnel Experiment.

## Day 3: Understanding Variation and the Funnel Experiment

- [Day 3: Variation, the enemy of quality — the school bus story](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/01-variation-the-enemy-of-quality.html): Neave's school-bus story shows why variation matters more than the average, then Deming's Western Electric account introduces common and special causes.
- [Day 3: The Ford Motor Company shafts that got better with less](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/02-at-the-ford-motor-company.html): A Ford Motor Company case study: turning off an expensive automatic compensation device reduced variation and improved quality, not the reverse.
- [Day 3: Why histograms hide a process's story over time](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/03-the-importance-of-time.html): Two datasets share an identical histogram but opposite trends over time, showing why histograms alone can't tell you if a process is in control.
- [Day 3: The 'sales data' were actually dice throws all along](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/04-more-on-the-sales-data.html): The reveal: Day 2's monthly sales figures were really dice throws. A control chart shows the management's story-building was applied to pure noise.
- [Day 3: How control limits are computed, using moving ranges](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/05-how-do-we-compute-control-limits.html): Why control limits are computed from moving ranges rather than the standard deviation, a method that stays useful even when a process is out of control.
- [Day 3: Six real processes, in and out of statistical control](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/06-six-processes.html): Twelve control charts from six very different processes — dice, coins, pulse rate, manufacturing, trade deficits — comparing stable and unstable behaviour.
- [Day 3: 'Hugging the Central Line' — Deming's fear-driven fudge](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/07-a-favourite-example.html): Deming's favourite example: a control chart 'hugging the Central Line' too tightly reveals an inspector fudging figures out of fear of a plant closure.
- [Day 3: Interpreting control charts needs judgment, not just rules](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/08-control-chart-and-brain.html): Why reading a control chart well means combining the rules with judgment and subject knowledge, not mechanically checking if points cross a line.
- [Day 3: The Six Processes revisited — spotting special causes](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/09-the-six-processes-revisited.html): Extending the Six Processes charts to 48 points each, tracing exactly where and how special causes show up, from a beta-blocker to a financial crisis.
- [Day 3: Introducing the Funnel Experiment](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/10-introduction-to-the-funnel-experiment.html): Introducing Lloyd Nelson's Funnel Experiment and Neave's simplified one-dimensional version, built from a numbered track, a funnel, a marble and dice.
- [Day 3: Funnel Experiment Rules 1 and 2 — doing nothing wins](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/11-the-first-two-rules-of-the-funnel.html): Major Activity 3-h: running the Funnel Experiment's Rules 1 and 2 shows that leaving the process alone beats constantly compensating for each result.
- [Day 3: Funnel Experiment Rules 3 and 4 — tampering gets worse](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/12-rules-3-and-4-of-the-funnel.html): Rules 3 and 4 of the Funnel Experiment: symmetric placement produces a zig-zag disaster, while chasing the last result makes the process drift away.
- [Day 3: Summary — tampering vs improving the system](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-03/13-summary.html): Day 3's summary: comparing all four Rules of the Funnel confirms that tampering with a stable process only makes things worse than leaving it alone.

## Day 4: The Joiner Triangle and the 14 Points (Part 1)

- [Day 4: Introduction to the Joiner Triangle and the 14 Points](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-04/01-introduction.html): Day 4 opens with the 1981 Hewlett-Packard origins of Deming's 14 Points, then introduces the Joiner Triangle that ties them together.
- [Day 4: The Joiner Triangle's three foundations explained](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-04/02-the-joiner-triangle.html): The Joiner Triangle's three foundations — Scientific Approach, All One Team, Obsession With Quality — with activities tying each to real workplaces.
- [Day 4: The First Project — working through the 14 Points and Deadly Diseases](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-04/03-the-first-project.html): How to tackle the First Project: pairing each of Deming's 14 Points and five Deadly Diseases with the Joiner Triangle's three foundations.
- [Deming's 14 Points 1–6: constancy of purpose to instituting training](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-04/04-points-1-to-6.html): Deming's first six Points: constancy of purpose, new philosophy, ending mass inspection, lowest-tender contracts, continual improvement, training.

## Day 5: The Joiner Triangle, The 14 Points (Part 2), and The Deadly Diseases

- [Day 5: Introduction to Points 7–14 and the Deadly Diseases](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-05/01-introduction.html): Day 5 continues the First Project with the remaining eight of Deming's 14 Points and the five Deadly Diseases, plus his 1984 video on the Diseases.
- [Deming's 14 Points 7–14: leadership to top management commitment](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-05/02-points-7-to-14.html): Points 7–14 of Deming's 14 Points: leadership, driving out fear, breaking barriers, eliminating targets, pride of workmanship, education, top management.
- [Deming's five Deadly Diseases of Western management](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-05/03-the-deadly-diseases.html): Deming's five Deadly Diseases — lack of constancy, short-termism, performance appraisal, job-hopping, visible-figures-only thinking — in his own words.

## Day 6: Gallery Furniture and Other True Stories

- [Day 6: Introduction to the Gallery Furniture case study](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-06/01-introduction.html): Day 6 turns from theory to practice: score your own organisation against the 14 Points, then meet the Gallery Furniture case study.
- [The Gallery Furniture story: Mack McIngvale's Deming transformation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-06/02-gallery-furniture.html): Jim "Mack" McIngvale's own account of taking Gallery Furniture from commission-driven chaos to a Deming-based, salaried, salesperson-empowered business.
- [Day 6: Scoring Gallery Furniture's before-and-after transformation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-06/03-activity-6b.html): Major Activity 6-b: score Gallery Furniture against the 14 Points and Deadly Diseases before and after Deming, then compare with your own organisation.
- [Day 6: true stories of targets gone wrong, from the NHS to policing](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-06/04-more-true-stories.html): Ten stories of numerical targets backfiring — hospital waiting lists, police response times, school league tables, Stafford Hospital, fudged crime figures.

## Day 7: Targets, Appraisals, and Other Obstacles

- [Day 7: Introduction to targets, appraisals and performance indicators](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-07/01-introduction.html): Neave opens Day 7's look at targets, appraisals, quotas, specifications and league tables — the obstacles that undermine Deming's management theory.
- [Day 7: The three kinds of numerical targets](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-07/02-numerical-targets.html): Neave distinguishes facts of life, numbers for guidance, and numbers for judgment — only the last, used for reward or punishment, is Deming's real target.
- [Day 7: Why performance indicators can't indicate performance](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-07/03-performance-indicators.html): Performance indicators are singular and local, but performance is multi-faceted and systemic — plus how Peter Scholtes phased out appraisal, not banned it.
- [Day 7: More true stories of targets gone wrong](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-07/04-many-more-true-stories.html): Real accounts of nail factories, railway timetable padding, spiky chairs and fudged KPIs — how numerical targets invite gaming rather than improvement.
- [Day 7: The 13th obstacle — meeting specifications isn't enough](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-07/05-thirteenth-obstacle.html): A hands-on temperature exercise introduces the Taguchi loss function, showing why conformance to specification is a crude, illogical measure of quality.
- [Day 7: Reflecting on the Taguchi loss function](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-07/06-taguchi-reflections.html): Why the Taguchi loss function justifies continual improvement and centring a process, while conformance-to-specifications thinking says 'good enough'.
- [Day 7: Major Activity — the 16 obstacles to transformation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-07/07-major-activity.html): Working through Deming's full 'parade of obstacles', from hope for instant pudding to the fallacy of zero defects, relating each to your own organisation.

## Day 8: A New Climate

- [Day 8: Introducing the New Climate — joy, innovation, cooperation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-08/01-introduction.html): Neave pivots from Day 7's bad practices to the New Climate of Joy in Work, Innovation and Cooperation, tracing its roots to his 1988 journal article.
- [Day 8: Joy in Work](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-08/02-joy-in-work.html): An activity reflecting on how much Joy in Work exists in your organisation, what obstructs it, and what could be done to encourage more of it.
- [Day 8: Innovation — not just improvement](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-08/03-innovation.html): An activity exploring innovation in your organisation: what obstructs it, what it costs to lack it, and what could encourage more of it.
- [Day 8: Cooperation — win-win, the backbone of the new philosophy](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-08/04-cooperation.html): An activity on cooperation in your organisation, the longest of Day 8's three New Climate chapters and Deming's alternative to internal competition.
- [Day 8: Introducing the cooperation Major Activity](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-08/05-introduction-to-the-major-activity.html): Walking through Fred Herr's Areas A, B, C exercise from DemDim — the same options score zero net gain under self-interest but a gain under cooperation.
- [Day 8: Major Activity — cooperation Tables One to Five](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-08/06-major-activity.html): Building your own five-table cooperation exercise, showing how New Climate cooperative decisions free up resource that Old Climate self-interest wastes.

## Day 9: A System ... of Profound Knowledge

- [Day 9: Introduction to a System of Profound Knowledge](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-09/01-introduction.html): Neave introduces Day 9's two halves: appreciating an organisation as a system this morning, then the System of Profound Knowledge itself this afternoon.
- [Day 9: Deming's Organisation Viewed as a System flow diagram](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-09/02-a-system.html): Tracing Deming's famous flow diagram back to Shewhart's 1939 circle of specification, production and inspection — 'the spark that turned Japan around'.
- [Day 9: Organisation charts vs Deming's flow diagram](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-09/03-activity-9c-and-organisation-charts.html): Why the conventional 'train-wreck' organisation chart assigns blame while Deming's horizontal flow diagram shows everyone their job and whom it serves.
- [Day 9: Major Activity — mapping your organisation as a system](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-09/04-major-activity.html): A five-stage activity building a macro flow diagram of your own organisation, starting with a practice diagram of a system of medical care.
- [Day 9: Preparing for the System of Profound Knowledge](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-09/05-of-profound-knowledge.html): Neave outlines the four-step procedure for the Second Project on Days 10-11, and the three sources: Deming's 1990 text, DemDim, and The New Economics.
- [Day 9: Four introductions to the System of Profound Knowledge](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-09/06-introductions-to-the-system.html): Scholtes's diagram, DemDim's chapter, Balaji Reddie's newspaper articles, and Deming's own May 1990 text — four routes into his final teaching.
- [Day 9: Out-of-hours preparation for the Second Project](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-09/07-out-of-hours.html): Homework before Day 10: revisiting the 14 Points and Deadly Diseases, and rehearsing the Second Project's four-step procedure for the coming two days.

## Day 10: A System of Profound Knowledge — Parts A and B

- [Day 10: Beginning the Second Project on the System of Profound Knowledge](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-10/01-second-project.html): Neave opens the Second Project, guiding you to explain each item to an imagined 'interested friend' unfamiliar with Deming's terms.
- [Day 10: Part A — Appreciation for a system](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-10/02-appreciation-for-a-system.html): Deming's definition of a system, the aim of 'everybody to gain', and why a business needs even more teamwork than an orchestra or a bowling team.
- [Day 10: Activity 10-a — rating the Points and Diseases against Part A](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-10/03-activity-10a.html): Scoring, on a 0–5 scale, how strongly each of the 14 Points and five Deadly Diseases connects to your new understanding of Appreciation for a System.
- [Day 10: Part B — Some knowledge of theory of variation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-10/04-theory-of-variation.html): Neave's blood-pressure story introduces stable systems, common and special causes, and the two costly mistakes of tampering with a process.
- [Day 10: Activity 10-b — rating the Points and Diseases against Part B](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-10/05-activity-10b.html): Scoring the strength of the links between the 14 Points, the five Deadly Diseases, and your new understanding of Theory of Variation.
- [Day 10: Out-of-hours preparation for Parts C and D](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-10/06-out-of-hours-note.html): Halfway through the Second Project, Neave guides your preparation on Balaji's Preludes and DemDim before tackling Theory of Knowledge and Psychology.

## Day 11: A System of Profound Knowledge — Parts C and D

- [Day 11: Introducing Parts C and D of the System of Profound Knowledge](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/01-introduction.html): Neave introduces Theory of Knowledge and Knowledge of Psychology, both tracing back to the work of Walter Shewhart.
- [Day 11: Part C, Area 1 — Prediction](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/02-theory-of-knowledge-prediction.html): Why 'management is action based on prediction', and Deming's Cedar Crest address on the difference between information and knowledge.
- [Day 11: Part C, Area 2 — Theory and learning](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/03-theory-of-knowledge-theory-and-learning.html): The Shewhart (PDSA) Cycle and Bill Scherkenbach's seven-word theory of knowledge: theory, question, data, prediction, knowledge, action, wisdom.
- [Day 11: Part C, Area 3 — Operational definitions](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/04-theory-of-knowledge-operational-definitions.html): What makes a definition 'operational' — illustrated with punctual, unemployed and clean — plus why Deming said there is no true value of anything.
- [Day 11: Activity 11-a — rating the Points and Diseases against Part C](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/05-activity-11a.html): Scoring links between the 14 Points, the Deadly Diseases, and Theory of Knowledge — now also considering how the Points guide how to act.
- [Day 11: Part D — Knowledge of psychology](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/06-knowledge-of-psychology.html): Intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation and overjustification — and Deming's case for why pay, above a certain level, is not a motivator.
- [Day 11: Activity 11-b — rating the Points and Diseases against Part D](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/07-activity-11b.html): The final ratings activity of the Second Project, linking the 14 Points and Deadly Diseases to Knowledge of Psychology.
- [Day 11: Coda — completing the Second Project](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-11/08-coda.html): Neave closes the Second Project and asks you to find coloured pens ahead of Day 12's radar diagram activity.

## Day 12: Bringing It All Together — and Making It Happen

- [Day 12: Overture — bringing it all together](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/01-overture.html): An overview of Day 12's seven sections, from your radar diagram and Peter Scholtes's wisdom to leadership for the transformation and the epilogue.
- [Day 12: Your radar diagram — visualising the Second Project's scores](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/02-your-radar-diagram.html): Activity 12-a turns your 19 sets of 0–5 scores from Days 10–11 into a radar diagram revealing which parts of Profound Knowledge need more work.
- [Day 12: Wisdom from Peter Scholtes — profound knowledge in practice](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/03-wisdom-from-peter-scholtes.html): Peter Scholtes's Motor Equipment Operation story, an interlinks activity on his System of Profound Knowledge diagram, and his parody 'Profound Trouble'.
- [Day 12: 'But what can I do?' — guidance for staff and middle managers](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/04-but-what-can-i-do.html): Dave Young's practical guidance for those who feel too junior to act, built on Deming's 'transformation of the individual' from The New Economics.
- [Day 12: Leadership for the transformation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/05-leadership-for-the-transformation.html): Deming's expanded 'Modern Principles of Leadership' — 14 suggestions for replacing the annual performance review with genuine leadership.
- [Day 12: Activity 12-d — applying the leadership guidance to your role](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/06-activity-12d.html): Turning Sections 3 and 4's guidance on staff, management and leadership into a plan of action for your own position and organisation.
- [Day 12: Major Activity 12-e — drafting Dr Deming's report to your organisation](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/07-major-activity-12e.html): The final Major Activity: imagine Dr Deming touring your organisation, draft his report to the Chief Executive, then plan the changes it calls for.
- [Day 12: Epilogue — 'I have done my best'](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/days/day-12/08-epilogue.html): The Deming of America's extract on the Emperor of Japan's medal, and the five words with which Deming ended every four-day seminar.

## Optional

- [Glossary: common cause, special cause, and the course's core terms](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/glossary.html): Seven recurring terms defined verbatim from Neave's prose — common cause, special cause, PDSA cycle, operational definition — each linked to first use.
- [Appendix: the out-of-hours preparation checklist](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/00-welcome.html): A day-by-day list of what to print or prepare ahead of Days 2 through 12, cross-linked to where each task is explained in the day it serves.
- [Day 1 appendix: why control charts are missing from statistics courses](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/01-day-1.html): Neave's fuller answer to the 'first paradox' — how Shewhart's empirical 3σ-limits diverge from Mathematical Statistics' reliance on normality.
- [Day 2 appendix: Red Beads control limits and Dave Kerr's wrap-up](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/02-day-2.html): Worked control-limit calculations for the statisticians' and Spaniards' Red Beads data, plus Dave Kerr's wrap-up brief on the experiment's lessons.
- [Day 3 appendix: the Funnel Experiment's four Rules, worked through](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/03-day-3.html): Neave's simulation-based discussion of the Funnel Experiment's Rules 1–4 — zig-zag and wandering effects — with delegate-submitted real-world examples.
- [Day 4 appendix: continuous vs continual improvement, and the Joiner Triangle](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/04-day-4.html): Answers to Day 4's Joiner Triangle activities, plus why Deming chose 'continual' over 'continuous' improvement and why removing a bad practice needs care.
- [Day 5 appendix: cross-referencing Points 7–14 and the Deadly Diseases](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/05-day-5.html): Neave links Points 7–14 and the five Deadly Diseases to the Joiner Triangle's three corners — Obsession With Quality, All One Team, Scientific Approach.
- [Day 7 appendix: Deming's 16 Obstacles to the Transformation, in full](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/06-day-7.html): The full text of Deming's Major Activity 7–i — his 16 obstacles to transformation, from 'hope for instant pudding' to the fallacy of zero defects.
- [Day 9 appendix: an organisation-chart activity and a medical-research diagram](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/07-day-9.html): A short answer hint for Activity 9–c on job obstacles, plus the flow diagram used in Day 9's medical-research organisation Major Activity.
- [Day 10 appendix: Appreciation for a System meets the Joiner Triangle](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/08-day-10.html): Neave's answers to Activities 10–a and 10–b, tracing how the System of Profound Knowledge's first two parts connect back to Day 4's Joiner Triangle.
- [Day 11 appendix: Theory of Knowledge and Psychology meet the Joiner Triangle](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/09-day-11.html): Neave's answers to Activities 11–a and 11–b, connecting the System of Profound Knowledge's Theory of Knowledge and Psychology parts to the Joiner Triangle.
- [Optional Extras: deeper control-charting material beyond the main course](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/optional-extras/00-introduction.html): A guided introduction to six optional parts on control-charting in more depth — from Funnel Experiment charts to a crash course in conventional Statistics.
- [Optional Extras Part A: control charts for the Funnel Experiment](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/optional-extras/01-part-a-funnel-charts.html): Draw and interpret control charts for your own Funnel Experiment data across all four Rules, then compare against Neave's two computer-simulated runs.
- [Optional Extras Part B: the X-bar-R chart for a-few-at-a-time data](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/optional-extras/02-part-b-subgrouped.html): How to build X-bar and R charts from subgrouped data, worked through with the historic hand-drawn Japanese control chart of a cigar-lighter shell.
- [Optional Extras Part C: the Deming/Shewhart and conventional-statistics divide](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/optional-extras/03-part-c-ne-er-twain.html): Why control charts don't depend on normality or probability theory, despite what a conventionally-trained statistician believes — and how to talk to one.
- [Optional Extras Part D: a crash course in conventional Statistics](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/optional-extras/04-part-d-crash-course.html): Histograms, probability distributions, the normal distribution, the Central Limit Theorem, confidence intervals, and hypothesis tests, in plain terms.
- [Optional Extras Part E: is there anything normal about control charts?](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/optional-extras/05-part-e-normality.html): Two computer simulations disproving the claims that control-chart constants require normal data and that a 3σ signal has a 0.0027 probability.
- [Optional Extras Part F: why control-chart constants are what they are](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/optional-extras/06-part-f-technical.html): Simulation evidence for choosing a baseline length, proofs behind the control-chart constants, and tables of the binomial and normal distributions.
- [Appendix: debunking the six-sigma '3.4 parts per million' superstition](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/10-optional-extras.html): Neave's rewrite of his 'More Superstitions' article, written for Balaji Reddie — where the six-sigma '3.4 parts per million' figure really comes from.
- [Balaji Reddie's Preludes: introducing the System of Profound Knowledge](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/00-introduction.html): Balaji Reddie's four introductory Preludes to Appreciation for a System, Statistical Thinking, Learning, and Psychology, plus a closing Coda.
- [Prelude A: understanding a system, by Balaji Reddie](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/01-prelude-a-system.html): What makes a tiger, an orchestra, or a company a system — aim, interconnection, cause and effect far apart, and why ranking people makes no sense.
- [Prelude B: understanding statistical thinking, by Balaji Reddie](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/02-prelude-b-statistical-thinking.html): Common cause vs special cause explained through a commute-to-work example, plus two true stories of workers wrongly blamed for a process's own variation.
- [Prelude C: understanding learning, by Balaji Reddie](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/03-prelude-c-learning.html): A father, a scooter, and a boy's evolving theory of what makes it start — Balaji Reddie's illustration of how theory turns information into real knowledge.
- [Prelude D: does pay motivate? by Balaji Reddie](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/04-prelude-d-people.html): Why Deming said 'pay is not a motivator', competing with versus competing against, and why extrinsic rewards can extinguish the intrinsic desire to learn.
- [Coda: Balaji Reddie's closing reflection on the Preludes](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/05-coda.html): Deming's own vision of the transformed world — 'everyone will win; no losers' — and a closing reflection on carrying his teaching forward.
- [Some lessons from history: Kaizen, Quality Circles, and Six Sigma misread](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/06-lessons-from-history.html): Balaji Reddie on how Kaizen, Quality Circles, Just In Time, and Six Sigma get misunderstood when copied without Deming's underlying theory.
- [India's missed opportunity with Deming, by Balaji Reddie](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/contributions-balaji-reddie/07-indias-missed-opportunity.html): How Prime Minister Nehru's meeting with Deming came to nothing, and how one Lucknow school is teaching Deming's principles to children today.
- [Appendix: references, sources, and further reading](https://deming.leedurbin.co.nz/content/appendix/11-references-and-sources.html): The course's full bibliography — books, BDA booklets, videos, and contact links for Deming and Shewhart's own writing plus the wider Deming community.
